mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-week improvement in TRANSIT mobility signals the return of commuting routines that lifts weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.6 at t-2w to -28.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to improve but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility exceeds +10 for at least one week, outdoor leisure activity spills over into adjacent retail and hospitality, driving higher RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS > 10 for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 11.9 at t-0w and 10.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays above 10 but the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint week-on-week increases in TRANSIT and PARKS indicate broadening local mobility for both commuting and leisure, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and PARKS both rise week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -29.1 at t-1w to -28.0 at t-0w and PARKS rose from 10.1 to 11.9
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and PARKS both rise in a week but the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-restriction reopening regime, a WORKPLACES level below -30 that stops worsening signals removal of mobility constraints, allowing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was -34.4 at t-0w versus -33.9 at t-1w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -30 with week-on-week change > -1 but RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is not above the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: As PARKS mobility rises above baseline while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline, summer outdoor and holiday behavior diverts spending away from retail-and-recreation locations, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 11.9 and RESIDENTIAL was 5.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS rises above 10 and RESIDENTIAL stays above 5 but RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM above -26 for two consecutive weeks signals restored essential-errand routines, which lift nearby retail footfall and raise RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > -26 for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was -24.0 at t-1w and -24.6 at t-0w, both above -26
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains above -26 for two weeks but the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -30 after two weeks below -30 signals easing of travel constraints, which drives higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT > -30 after being < -30 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -33.6 at t-2w and -28.0 at t-0w, crossing -30
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -30 but the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES remains below -30 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5, sustained work-from-home shifts spending away from office-centric retail, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES < -30 and RESIDENTIAL > 5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES was -34.4 and RESIDENTIAL was 5.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -30 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 but RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is higher than the last 28-day mean.
